Roasted Marry Me Cauliflower (With Creamy Tuscan Sauce)

By Sarah Bond, BS Nutrition, MS Sensory Science, Published Oct 13, 2026

Leave a Review

45 minutes

Serves 4 servings

No Comments

Instaread

Marry Me Cauliflower is big, char-edged roasted florets folded into a garlicky sun-dried tomato cream sauce that’s smoky, rich, and flecked with fresh basil. The cauliflower roasts while the sauce simmers on the stove, so dinner is on the table in about 30 minutes with just two pans.

Marry me chicken got all the attention, and vegetarians got a side salad. That never sat right with me, so I keep giving the creamy Tuscan treatment to plants. Cauliflower was one of the easiest swaps yet.

Hot take: roasting first isn’t optional. Roast big florets over high heat until the edges caramelize, then fold them into the sauce at the very end.

My sensory science background makes me a little obsessive about this pairing. Caramelized cauliflower edges and smoked paprika both bring deep, smoky, slightly bitter roasted notes, so they amplify each other.

Why You’ll Want to Make This Every Week

  • Smoked paprika plus caramelized cauliflower equals deep, campfire-adjacent flavor.
  • Spoon it over quinoa, farro, or pasta, or just grab a hunk of crusty bread.
  • Leftovers worth fighting over. My family does.

Key Ingredients

  • Cauliflower: Look for a heavy head with tight, creamy-white curds.
  • Sun-dried tomatoes: Oil-packed tomatoes are already plump and tender, so they soften fully in a 5-minute simmer, while dry-packed ones stay leathery unless you rehydrate them first. A spoonful of the jar oil in the pan adds even more tomato flavor!
  • Heavy cream: Heavy cream, not half-and-half, is what gives this sauce its rich body. The higher fat also makes it more stable over heat, so it’s less likely to break while it sits on low.
  • Fresh basil: I wouldn’t swap in dried basil here because its flavor is such an important part of the dish. Stir it in at the end, since basil’s aroma compounds are volatile and fade fast with heat.
  • Smoked paprika: The quiet hero. It echoes the charred cauliflower edges, so the smoky flavor carries through every bite instead of living only on the browned bits.
  • Parmesan: Grate it from a block, because pre-shredded parmesan is coated in anti-caking agents that can make the sauce gritty. For a strictly vegetarian dish, choose a parmesan-style cheese made with microbial rennet, since traditional Parmigiano-Reggiano uses animal rennet.

Ways to Change It Up

  • Add chickpeas: Toss a can of drained, patted-dry chickpeas onto the sheet pan with the cauliflower for extra protein and chew. If you want chickpeas front and center, my Marry Me Chickpeas make them the star.
  • Wilt in greens: Stir a couple of handfuls of baby spinach or chopped kale into the warm sauce right before the cauliflower goes in.
  • Turn up the heat: Double the red pepper flakes or add a pinch of cayenne with the spices.

What to Serve With Marry Me Cauliflower

On busy weeknights, this lands on our table over a scoop of quinoa or farro with a slice of crusty bread on the side for mopping up the sauce. Pasta works great too, or tear into my homemade naan for dragging through every last drop.

For something crisp and sharp to cut the cream, add my Vegetarian Caesar Salad or my Roasted Brussels Sprouts with Balsamic and Garlic, whose tangy glaze balances all that richness.

Roasted Marry Me Cauliflower (With Creamy Tuscan Sauce)

By: Sarah Bond
Prep: 15 minutes minutes
Cook: 30 minutes minutes
Total: 45 minutes minutes
Servings: 4 servings
My marry me cauliflower has char-edged roasted florets in a garlicky sun-dried tomato cream sauce with fresh basil. Smoky, rich, and ready in 30 minutes!

Ingredients 

  • 1 large head cauliflower, cut into big chunks
  • 2 Tbsp oil, 30 mL
  • 2 Tbsp unsalted butter, 28 g
  • 4 cloves garlic, minced
  • ½ tsp each salt, oregano, crushed red pepper flakes, smoked paprika
  • ¼ tsp ground black pepper
  • ½ cup sun-dried tomatoes, packed in oil, roughly chopped, 55g
  • 1 cup heavy cream, can sub half-and-half, 236 mL
  • ½ cup grated parmesan, 50 g
  • 2 Tbsp chopped fresh basil

Instructions 

  • Cauliflower: Preheat oven to 425°F (218°C). Cut 1 large head cauliflower into large chunks (a little bigger than bite-sizes).
    Toss them onto a parchment-lined baking sheet, drizzle with 2 Tbsp oil, and toss everything to coat. Bake for about 20 minutes. Flip all the pieces over, and then continue baking for another 5 minutes. They should be a bit charred and browned at the edges.
  • Flavor Base: Melt 2 Tbsp unsalted butter in a large saute pan. Add 4 cloves garlic (minced), ½ tsp each salt, oregano, crushed red pepper flakes, smoked paprika, and ¼ tsp ground black pepper. Cook until garlic is soft and fragrant, about 1 minute.
  • Sauce: Add ½ cup sun-dried tomatoes (roughly chopped) and 1 cup heavy cream. Gently simmer until hot, about 5 minutes.
    Once hot, reduce heat to the lowest setting, cover, and keep it warm on the stove until cauliflower is finished.
  • Stir: Once cauliflower is finished cooking, stir in ½ cup grated parmesan, 2 Tbsp chopped fresh basil, and cooked cauliflower.
    Try not to overstir, which will cause the cauliflower florets to break.
  • Serve warm over pasta, quinoa, or by itself with crusty bread for dipping!

Notes

Store leftovers in an airtight glass container in the fridge for 3 to 4 days. The cauliflower softens as it sits and the sauce thickens, so reheat gently in a covered skillet over low heat with a splash of cream, milk, or water, folding carefully. The microwave works too: use 30-second bursts at medium power so the sauce doesn’t split.
I don’t recommend freezing. Cream sauces tend to turn grainy after thawing, and the cauliflower goes watery and limp.
To get ahead, roast the cauliflower up to a day early and refrigerate it. Rewarm it in a hot oven for a few minutes, then fold it into freshly made sauce.
Can I Make Marry Me Cauliflower Vegan? Yes. Swap the butter for vegan butter or olive oil, the heavy cream for full-fat canned coconut milk or cashew cream, and the parmesan for vegan parmesan or 2 to 3 Tbsp nutritional yeast. Coconut milk adds a faint sweetness that plays nicely with the sun-dried tomatoes, while cashew cream is the most neutral option.
Can I Use Frozen Cauliflower? You can, but fresh is the better choice here. Frozen florets release a lot of water, so they steam more than they char, and they’re often cut small, which means more breakage. If you go frozen, roast straight from the freezer on a well-spaced pan and add 10 to 15 minutes, until the edges brown.
Why Did My Sauce Turn Grainy or Oily? Usually it’s heat. Parmesan stirred into a bubbling sauce can seize into clumps, and cream that boils hard can separate. Keep the sauce at a gentle simmer, drop it to low before adding the cheese, and use freshly grated parmesan. If it does separate, whisk in a splash of warm cream off the heat to bring it back together.
